race_context: Blackford County Schools, based in Hartford City, serves most of Blackford County; part of the county lies in Jay School Corporation, whose voters choose Jay board members instead {hcnt_ev}. State enrollment counts were 1,471 students in 2023-24, 1,412 in 2024-25 and 1,384 in 2025-26, down from 1,586 in 2018-19 {idoe_enroll}. The state ballot list calls the office 'Blackford Community School Board' {in_list}.
Superintendent: Chad Yencer has led the district since 2017. The Indiana Association of Public School Superintendents named him its 2025-26 District VI Superintendent of the Year {hcnt_yencer}.

The board has five members: three elected from districts and two at large {hcnt_2016}{hcnt_2018}. The District 1-3 seats were filled in 2018 and 2022, and the two at-large seats in 2020 and 2024; Troy Kaufman and Nikki Gorrell won the at-large seats in 2024 {hcnt_2018}{enr_2022}{enr_2020}{enr_2024}. Phil Jones is board president and Kaufman was vice president as of March 2026 {hcnt_yencer}{hcnt_pac}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: Districts 1, 2 and 3, one seat each, matching the state list {in_list}{hcnt_ev}. District 1 is open because incumbent Jimmy Lytle is not seeking another term; Melinda Huber and Kyle J Pitts are running. District 2 incumbent Scott Malott is unopposed. District 3 incumbent Phil Jones faces Kerra Armstrong {hcnt_ev}.

Party labels: this is the first Blackford school board election in which candidates could declare a party. Jones and Malott did not; Pitts and Armstrong filed as Republicans and Huber as an Independent {hcnt_ev}{ic_list}.

Facilities: in March 2026 the district broke ground on a $19.5 million performing arts center with a 700-seat auditorium at Blackford Junior-Senior High School ($21.5 million in total project cost), set to open in May 2027. Yencer said it is being built 'with no increase in taxes' because bonds from earlier projects are retiring. The board began serious work on the project in August 2024 {hcnt_pac}. Yencer said the district had done $23 million in other work, including roofs and HVAC upgrades {hcnt_pac}.

Academics: Blackford's IREAD third-grade reading pass rate rose to 91.8% in 2026 from 81% the year before, the biggest gain in the News-Times' coverage area and the third straight year of gains (72.5% in 2023) {hcnt_iread}. In February 2026 Yencer reported higher SAT scores at the junior-senior high school and an expansion of Blackford Primary's preschool from one classroom to five {hcnt_city}.
Budget: this guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Blackford County Schools, and no operating or safety referendum.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign website for any Blackford candidate. The district website could not be loaded.
